Access the web interface at 'https://localhost:8834', register for a free Essentials activation code by email, and complete the initial plugin download (which can take a while on first run).

quiz.question: What is the main difference between Nessus Essentials and Nessus Professional?
options: Essentials is free but limited to 16 IPs; Professional is paid and unlimited
Professional cannot be installed on Kali Linux
quiz.explanation: Nessus Essentials is a free, IP-limited edition great for learning and small labs, while Professional removes the IP cap for enterprise use at a paid licence.

cards.title: Scan Policies & Templates
cards.body: Nessus offers pre-built templates: 'Basic Network Scan' for a general sweep, 'Advanced Scan' for full customisation, 'Web Application Tests' for web-specific checks, and 'Credentialed Patch Audit' which logs into the target with provided credentials for a far more thorough, lower-noise assessment than an unauthenticated scan.

cards.title: Reading Reports & Severity Ratings
cards.body: Nessus ranks every finding by severity — Critical, High, Medium, Low, and Info — based on CVSS scores, and each finding includes a description, affected hosts, and specific remediation steps. Prioritise Critical and High findings first; reports can be exported as HTML, CSV, or Nessus (.nessus) format for further processing in other tools.

quiz.question: Why does a Credentialed Patch Audit typically give more accurate results than an unauthenticated scan?
options: It scans faster than other templates
It logs into the target with valid credentials, allowing a much deeper, more accurate check of installed software and patches
It doesn't require a Nessus licence
quiz.explanation: By authenticating to the target, Nessus can directly inspect installed software versions and patch levels rather than guessing from network responses alone, dramatically improving accuracy.

modules.title: Hydra Deep Dive — Brute Force Testing
modules.description: Going further with the online password-guessing tool for network login services.

cards.title: Hydra Overview
cards.body: Hydra (THC-Hydra) is a fast, parallelised online password-cracking tool supporting dozens of protocols, including SSH, FTP, HTTP(S) forms, RDP, SMB, MySQL, and Telnet. Unlike offline crackers (John the Ripper, Hashcat), Hydra attacks a live login service directly, one guess at a time over the network.

cards.title: Basic Syntax
cards.body: The general pattern is: 'hydra [options] -l <user>|-L <userlist> -p <pass>|-P <passlist> <target> <service>'. '-l' sets a single username, '-L' a username list. '-p' sets a single password, '-P' a password list (like rockyou.txt). '-t <n>' controls the number of parallel connection threads, and '-V' shows each login attempt verbosely.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between Hydra and an offline cracker like John the Ripper?
options: Hydra attacks a live network login service directly, while offline crackers work against a captured hash file
There is no difference between them
John the Ripper is faster than Hydra in every case
quiz.explanation: Hydra performs online brute-forcing against a live service over the network, whereas offline tools crack a hash file that has already been obtained.

cards.title: Command Examples Across Protocols
cards.body: SSH: 'hydra -l admin -P rockyou.txt ssh://192.168.1.10'. FTP: 'hydra -L users.txt -P passwords.txt ftp://192.168.1.10'. RDP: 'hydra -l administrator -P rockyou.txt rdp://192.168.1.10'. Web login form: 'hydra -l admin -P rockyou.txt 192.168.1.10 http-post-form "/login:user=^USER^&pass=^PASS^:F=failed"' — the F= string tells Hydra what failure text to detect.

cards.title: Defending Against Brute Force
cards.body: Account lockout policies (e.g. locking after 5 failed attempts) and rate limiting slow or stop Hydra-style attacks. Fail2ban on Linux automatically bans IPs showing repeated failed logins. Strong, unique passwords and MFA make brute-forcing impractical even with unlimited attempts — the same defences discussed for password cracking generally apply here.

quiz.question: What does the '-t' flag control in a Hydra command?
options: The number of parallel connection threads used during the attack
The type of hash being cracked
quiz.explanation: '-t' sets how many login attempts Hydra runs in parallel — higher values are faster but noisier and more likely to trigger lockouts or detection.

modules.title: SQLmap Deep Dive — Automated SQL Injection
modules.description: Detecting, exploiting, and understanding SQL injection at a deeper technical level.

cards.title: SQLmap Overview
cards.body: SQLmap is an open-source tool that automates detecting and exploiting SQL injection vulnerabilities across MySQL, PostgreSQL, MSSQL, Oracle, SQLite, and more. It can fingerprint the database, enumerate databases/tables/columns, dump data, and in some configurations read/write files on the underlying server — turning a slow manual process into a repeatable automated workflow.

cards.title: Detection & Injection Techniques
cards.body: SQLmap automatically tests multiple injection techniques: Boolean-based blind (inferring data from true/false responses), Time-based blind (inferring data from response delays), Error-based (extracting data directly from database error messages), UNION query-based (appending a UNION SELECT to pull extra data), and Stacked queries (executing multiple statements in one request, where supported).

quiz.question: What does 'Time-based blind' SQL injection rely on to extract data?
options: Measuring response time delays to infer true/false answers about the database
Directly viewing the database contents on screen
Uploading a file to the server
quiz.explanation: Time-based blind injection sends queries that intentionally delay the response (e.g. SLEEP()) only when a condition is true, letting the attacker infer data one bit at a time from timing alone.

cards.title: Command Examples
cards.body: 'sqlmap -u "http://target/page?id=1"' tests a URL parameter for injection. '--dbs' lists all databases once injection is confirmed. '-D shop --tables' lists tables within a specific database. '-D shop -T users --dump' dumps a specific table's contents. '--os-shell' attempts to get an interactive OS shell where the underlying database privileges allow it.

cards.title: Risk/Level Tuning & Ethical Use
cards.body: '--level' (1-5) controls how many injection points and payload variations SQLmap tests — higher levels are more thorough but slower and noisier. '--risk' (1-3) controls how aggressive/potentially destructive the payloads are; risk 3 includes payloads that could modify data and should never be used without explicit authorisation. SQLmap should only ever be run against systems you own or are contractually authorised to test.

quiz.question: What does increasing SQLmap's '--risk' level control?
options: How aggressive/potentially destructive the tested payloads are
quiz.explanation: Higher risk levels include payloads that are more likely to alter data or cause side effects, which is why authorisation and caution matter even more as risk increases.

modules.title: Aircrack-ng — Wireless Network Security
modules.description: Assessing Wi-Fi security by capturing and cracking WPA/WPA2 handshakes.

cards.title: WEP, WPA, WPA2 & WPA3
cards.body: WEP is an old, badly broken encryption standard, crackable in minutes regardless of password strength — it should never be used today. WPA improved on WEP but still had weaknesses. WPA2 (using AES-CCMP) has been the standard for years and is strong when a long, random passphrase is used. WPA3 is the newest standard, adding protections against offline dictionary attacks even for weaker passwords.

cards.title: The Aircrack-ng Suite
cards.body: Aircrack-ng is actually a suite of tools, not a single program: 'airmon-ng' enables monitor mode on a wireless adapter, 'airodump-ng' captures nearby wireless traffic and handshakes, 'aireplay-ng' sends deauthentication packets to force a handshake, and 'aircrack-ng' itself performs the offline cracking against a captured handshake file. All require a wireless adapter that supports monitor mode and packet injection.

quiz.question: Why should WEP encryption never be used today?
options: It's too slow for modern devices
It has fundamental cryptographic weaknesses that let it be cracked in minutes regardless of password strength
quiz.explanation: WEP's encryption design is fundamentally broken — it can be cracked quickly using well-known techniques no matter how strong the underlying password is.

cards.title: Monitor Mode & Capturing Traffic
cards.body: 'sudo airmon-ng start wlan0' puts the wireless adapter into monitor mode (often renaming it wlan0mon), letting it see all nearby wireless traffic rather than just traffic addressed to it. 'sudo airodump-ng wlan0mon' then lists nearby access points and connected clients, along with their BSSID, channel, and signal strength — the starting point for targeting a specific network.

cards.title: Deauth & Capturing the Handshake
cards.body: 'sudo airodump-ng -c <channel> --bssid <BSSID> -w capture wlan0mon' focuses capture on one target network and writes packets to a file. 'sudo aireplay-ng --deauth 5 -a <BSSID> wlan0mon' sends deauthentication packets, forcing a connected client to reconnect and produce a fresh WPA handshake, which airodump-ng then captures into the .cap file.

cards.title: Cracking the Handshake
cards.body: 'aircrack-ng -w rockyou.txt -b <BSSID> capture-01.cap' runs a dictionary attack against the captured handshake, trying each password in the wordlist until one produces a matching key. Because WPA2 handshakes require significant computation per guess, cracking speed is far slower than typical hash cracking — a strong, unique Wi-Fi password remains highly effective defence.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of sending deauthentication packets with aireplay-ng?
options: To permanently disconnect the target network from the internet
To force a connected client to reconnect, producing a fresh WPA handshake that can be captured
To speed up the cracking process itself
To change the Wi-Fi password automatically
quiz.explanation: Deauth packets kick a client off temporarily; when it automatically reconnects, it performs the WPA handshake again, giving the attacker a fresh capture to attempt cracking.

cards.title: Defending Wi-Fi Networks
cards.body: Use WPA3 where supported, or WPA2 with a long, random passphrase (16+ characters) rather than a dictionary word or common phrase. Change the default router admin credentials and SSID. Disable WPS, a feature with well-known PIN-guessing weaknesses. Enterprise networks should use WPA2/3-Enterprise with individual per-user authentication (802.1X) rather than one shared passphrase.

cards.title: Legal Boundaries for Wireless Testing
cards.body: Deauthentication attacks and handshake capture must only be performed against your own network or a network you have explicit written authorisation to test — deauthing someone else's Wi-Fi is both a disruption of service and, in most countries, illegal unauthorised access/interference. Wireless signals often extend beyond property lines, so always confirm the exact scope of any authorised test before starting.

quiz.question: Why is WPS considered a wireless security risk?
options: It slows down the Wi-Fi connection
It has well-known PIN-guessing weaknesses that can allow an attacker to recover the Wi-Fi password
quiz.explanation: WPS's PIN-based setup process has known flaws that let attackers brute-force the PIN relatively quickly, ultimately recovering the network's actual password — it should be disabled.

units.title: Unit 11: Kali Linux Installation & Cyber Law
units.description: Every way to get Kali Linux running, how to configure it after install, and the legal framework — Indian and global — that governs everything an ethical hacker does.

modules.title: Installing Kali Linux — Every Method
modules.description: From virtual machines to bare metal, USB, WSL, and the cloud.

cards.title: Overview of Installation Methods
cards.body: Kali Linux can be installed in several ways depending on your goal: Virtual Machine (safest for learning — isolated from your main OS), Bare Metal / Dual-Boot (best performance, full hardware access for Wi-Fi attacks), Live USB (portable, runs without installing, optional persistence), WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux — runs Kali tools inside Windows without a VM), and Cloud (a Kali instance on AWS/Azure/DigitalOcean for remote access).

cards.title: Hardware & Software Requirements
cards.body: Minimum: 20GB disk space, 2GB RAM (4GB+ recommended), and a 64-bit processor with virtualization support (Intel VT-x / AMD-V) enabled in BIOS/UEFI if running as a VM. For wireless attacks (Aircrack-ng), a USB Wi-Fi adapter that explicitly supports monitor mode and packet injection is required, since most laptop-built-in Wi-Fi cards do not support this when passed through to a VM.

quiz.question: Why is a Virtual Machine generally recommended as the first installation method for beginners?
options: It's the only way to install Kali at all
It isolates Kali from your main operating system, so mistakes can't damage your primary computer
quiz.explanation: A VM sandboxes Kali away from your host OS — if something breaks inside the VM, your main computer and its data remain completely unaffected.

cards.title: Using the Official Pre-Built Image
cards.body: The fastest, most reliable method: go to kali.org/get-kali → Virtual Machines, download the VMware or VirtualBox image (.7z), extract it fully, then in VMware choose 'Open a Virtual Machine' and select the .vmx file, or in VirtualBox use File → Import Appliance and select the .ova/.vbox file. Allocate at least 4GB RAM and 2 CPU cores in the VM settings before first boot.

cards.title: First Boot
cards.body: Power on the VM and log in with the default credentials kali/kali. Immediately change the password with 'passwd', then run 'sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade -y' to bring every package current. Install VMware Tools or VirtualBox Guest Additions for proper screen resolution and shared clipboard support, then take a clean snapshot as your restore point.

quiz.question: What are Kali's default login credentials on the official pre-built VM image?
quiz.explanation: The official pre-built Kali VM images use kali/kali as the default username and password — this must be changed immediately after first login.

cards.title: Bare-Metal Installation Steps
cards.body: 1. Download the Kali installer ISO from kali.org/get-kali. 2. Flash it to a USB drive using Rufus (Windows) or 'dd'/Balena Etcher (Linux/Mac). 3. Boot from the USB (enter BIOS/UEFI boot menu, usually F2/F12/Del at startup). 4. Follow the graphical installer: select language, keyboard, disk partitioning, and create a user account. 5. Complete installation, remove the USB, and reboot into Kali directly.

cards.title: Dual-Boot Considerations
cards.body: Dual-booting installs Kali alongside an existing OS (like Windows), letting you choose which to boot into. Critical precautions: back up all data first, shrink the existing partition (don't delete it) to free space for Kali, and let the installer create Kali's partitions in that free space. GRUB (Kali's bootloader) will then manage the boot menu for both operating systems — a partitioning mistake here can affect the existing OS, so back-ups are non-negotiable.

quiz.question: What is the single most important precaution before attempting a dual-boot Kali installation?
options: Backing up all existing data before touching any disk partitions
Installing Kali in a different language
quiz.explanation: Partitioning mistakes during a dual-boot setup can damage or delete data on the existing operating system, so a full backup beforehand is essential.

cards.title: Creating a Live USB
cards.body: A Live USB lets you boot straight into Kali from a USB drive on almost any computer, without installing anything to the internal disk. Download the Kali ISO, flash it to an 8GB+ USB drive with Rufus or Balena Etcher, then boot from the USB via the BIOS boot menu. By default, any changes made are lost when you shut down.

cards.title: Enabling Persistence
cards.body: Persistence lets a Live USB save files and settings between boots, using free space on the USB drive as a writable overlay. This requires creating a persistence partition (via 'gparted' or the Kali installer's advanced mode) labelled 'persistence', with a specific configuration file added to enable it. Once set up, choosing 'Live USB Persistence' at the boot menu keeps your changes across reboots.

quiz.question: By default, what happens to changes made while running Kali from a Live USB (without persistence)?
options: They are automatically saved to the cloud
They are lost when the computer shuts down
They are saved permanently to the internal hard disk
They are emailed to the user automatically
quiz.explanation: A standard Live USB runs entirely from temporary memory — any files or settings changed during the session disappear on shutdown unless persistence has been specifically configured.

cards.title: Kali on WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux)
cards.body: WSL lets Windows users run Kali's command-line tools directly inside Windows, without a VM or dual-boot. Install via PowerShell: 'wsl --install' (enables WSL), then 'wsl --install -d kali-linux' or install 'Kali Linux' from the Microsoft Store. This is convenient for command-line tools (Nmap, John the Ripper) but has limitations for GUI tools and raw wireless/packet-injection access compared to a full VM or bare-metal install.

cards.title: Kali in the Cloud
cards.body: Cloud providers like AWS, Azure, and DigitalOcean offer pre-built Kali images (or let you build one from the official ISO), giving a remotely accessible attacker machine with a static public IP — useful for engagements requiring an external vantage point. Cloud instances must be secured carefully (strong SSH keys, restricted firewall rules) since they are internet-facing by default, and cloud provider Acceptable Use Policies must be reviewed before running any active scanning from them.

quiz.question: What is a key limitation of running Kali via WSL compared to a full VM or bare-metal install?
options: WSL cannot run any command-line tools at all
WSL has limitations for GUI tools and raw wireless/packet-injection access
WSL requires a completely separate physical computer
WSL only works on Linux hosts
quiz.explanation: WSL is excellent for CLI-based tools but doesn't provide the same level of hardware access needed for GUI applications or wireless packet injection that a VM or bare-metal install offers.

modules.title: Post-Install Kali Configuration
modules.description: The essential steps to take right after installation, before any real work begins.

cards.title: Updating & Upgrading
cards.body: Immediately run 'sudo apt update' to refresh the package list, then 'sudo apt full-upgrade -y' to install every available update — Kali's tools and vulnerability databases change constantly, and an outdated install can miss recent CVEs or ship broken tool versions. Reboot afterward if a kernel update was installed: 'sudo reboot'.

cards.title: Changing Default Credentials & User Setup
cards.body: Change the default password immediately with 'passwd'. Recent Kali versions no longer use a default root account for daily use — create or confirm a standard user account and use 'sudo' for administrative tasks, following the same 'never stay logged in as root' principle covered in Linux fundamentals. Consider enabling full-disk encryption during install if the laptop will be carried outside a secure location.

quiz.question: Why is running a full system update the very first thing to do after installing Kali?
options: It makes the desktop wallpaper look better
Kali's tools and vulnerability databases change constantly, so an outdated install may miss recent CVEs or have broken tools
It's required to connect to Wi-Fi
quiz.explanation: Security tools rely on up-to-date vulnerability data and bug fixes — skipping the initial update leaves you working with stale, potentially broken tooling from the moment you start.

cards.title: Installing Missing Tools & Metapackages
cards.body: The default Kali image is streamlined, not every tool pre-installed. Metapackages bundle related tools: 'sudo apt install kali-linux-large' installs the full standard toolset, 'kali-tools-wireless' adds wireless-specific tools like the full Aircrack-ng suite, and 'kali-tools-web' adds web app testing tools. Individual tools can also be installed directly, e.g. 'sudo apt install nikto'.

cards.title: Configuring Network & Services
cards.body: Confirm network mode (Bridged for lab work needing a real LAN IP, NAT for general internet use) via VM settings. Verify connectivity with 'ip a' and 'ping 8.8.8.8'. Some services (like PostgreSQL for Metasploit) don't start automatically — start them as needed with 'sudo systemctl start postgresql', and use 'sudo systemctl enable <service>' to make a service start automatically on every future boot.

quiz.question: What does the 'kali-tools-wireless' metapackage do?
options: It installs the full set of wireless security tools, including the complete Aircrack-ng suite
It is required just to connect to any network
quiz.explanation: Metapackages bundle related tools together — 'kali-tools-wireless' adds the wireless-focused toolset like Aircrack-ng in one install command.

modules.title: Introduction to Cyber Law
modules.description: Why legal frameworks exist for cybersecurity, and India's foundational law.

cards.title: Why Cyber Law Exists
cards.body: Every technique covered throughout this course — scanning, exploitation, password cracking — is a criminal offence the moment it's performed without authorisation. Cyber law defines exactly where that line sits, what counts as a crime, and what penalties apply. For an ethical hacker, legal knowledge isn't optional background reading — it's what separates a career from a conviction.

cards.title: The Global Legal Landscape
cards.body: Nearly every country now has some form of computer crime legislation, though details vary widely: India has the Information Technology Act, 2000 (amended 2008). The United States has the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA). The European Union has GDPR (data protection) alongside national cybercrime laws. The Budapest Convention is an international treaty many countries have signed to harmonise cybercrime law and cross-border cooperation.

quiz.question: Why is legal knowledge considered essential for an ethical hacker, not just optional background?
options: It's only useful for passing exams
The exact same techniques taught in this course are criminal offences without proper authorisation, so knowing the legal boundaries is what keeps a career legitimate
Cyber laws don't actually apply to security professionals
It has no practical relevance to daily work
quiz.explanation: Technical skill and legal authorisation are inseparable in this field — the same scan or exploit is either a professional service or a crime depending entirely on whether it was authorised.

cards.title: Overview & Objectives
cards.body: The Information Technology Act, 2000 is India's primary law governing cybercrime, electronic commerce, and digital signatures. It was significantly amended in 2008 to add provisions for cyber terrorism, data protection, and expanded cybercrime definitions in response to evolving threats. It grants legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures, making them as valid as their paper equivalents (connecting back to the Non-Repudiation concepts covered earlier).

cards.title: Key Sections of the IT Act
cards.body: Section 43: penalises unauthorised access, damage, or data theft from a computer system (civil compensation). Section 66: covers computer-related offences (hacking) with criminal penalties. Section 66C: identity theft (fraudulent use of another's electronic signature/password). Section 66D: cheating by personation using computer resources (common in phishing cases). Section 67: publishing/transmitting obscene material in electronic form.

quiz.question: Which section of India's IT Act specifically addresses identity theft involving electronic signatures or passwords?
quiz.explanation: Section 66C specifically criminalises identity theft — the fraudulent use of another person's electronic signature, password, or other unique identification feature.

lessons.title: Cyber Crimes & Punishments under Indian Law

cards.title: Common Offences & Their Sections
cards.body: Unauthorised access/hacking a computer system: Section 66, up to 3 years imprisonment and/or a fine up to ₹5 lakh. Identity theft: Section 66C, up to 3 years and a fine up to ₹1 lakh. Phishing/cheating by personation: Section 66D, up to 3 years and a fine up to ₹1 lakh. Cyber terrorism (threatening India's unity, security, or sovereignty via computer resources): Section 66F, punishable with imprisonment up to life.

cards.title: Why Penalties Vary So Widely
cards.body: Penalties scale with intent and impact: accidental or minor unauthorised access is treated far more leniently than deliberate data theft, financial fraud, or acts endangering national security. This is exactly why 'scope of authorisation' matters so much in professional testing — the same technical action (e.g. accessing a server) can be a routine authorised test or a Section 66 offence purely based on whether permission existed.

quiz.question: Under India's IT Act, what is the maximum penalty for cyber terrorism (Section 66F)?
options: Imprisonment which may extend to life
quiz.explanation: Section 66F treats cyber terrorism as one of the most serious offences under the Act, carrying a maximum penalty of imprisonment for life given the potential threat to national security.

modules.title: Global Cyber Laws & Compliance
modules.description: Major international legal frameworks and the compliance standards organisations must follow.

cards.title: GDPR (European Union)
cards.body: The General Data Protection Regulation governs how personal data of EU residents is collected, stored, and processed, regardless of where the company is based. It requires organisations to report data breaches within 72 hours, gives individuals the 'right to be forgotten', and imposes massive penalties — up to €20 million or 4% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher, for serious violations.

cards.title: CFAA (United States) & the Budapest Convention
cards.body: The Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) is the primary US federal law criminalising unauthorised computer access, covering everything from hacking to distributing malware, with penalties scaling by intent and damage caused. The Budapest Convention on Cybercrime is the first international treaty addressing internet and computer crime, harmonising national laws and improving cross-border investigation cooperation among signatory countries.

quiz.question: Within how many hours must a data breach be reported under GDPR?
quiz.explanation: GDPR requires organisations to notify the relevant supervisory authority of a personal data breach within 72 hours of becoming aware of it.

cards.title: ISO 27001 & PCI-DSS
cards.body: ISO/IEC 27001 is an international standard for building and certifying an Information Security Management System (ISMS) — a structured, risk-based approach to protecting organisational data. PCI-DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) is mandatory for any organisation that stores, processes, or transmits credit card data, requiring specific controls like encryption, access restriction, and regular vulnerability scanning.

cards.title: HIPAA & Why Compliance Drives Pen Testing
cards.body: HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) governs the protection of patient health information in the US healthcare sector, with strict rules on data access, storage, and breach notification. Compliance standards like these are a major reason organisations commission penetration tests in the first place — many explicitly require regular, documented security testing as a condition of certification or audit.

quiz.question: Which compliance standard specifically governs the protection of credit card data?
quiz.explanation: PCI-DSS is specifically focused on protecting cardholder data and is mandatory for any organisation handling credit card transactions.

modules.title: Ethical & Professional Responsibility
modules.description: The legal duties, codes of ethics, and career paths that define professional ethical hacking.

cards.title: Authorization & Scope
cards.body: Every legal penetration test rests on a signed contract defining exactly what can be tested (scope), when (testing window), and how (rules of engagement — e.g. no denial-of-service, no social engineering unless explicitly included). Testing anything outside the agreed scope — even accidentally, like a misconfigured bridged network reaching a neighbouring system — can constitute an unauthorised access offence regardless of good intent.

cards.title: Responsible Disclosure & NDAs
cards.body: When a vulnerability is found — whether during an authorised test or a bug bounty — responsible disclosure means reporting it privately to the affected organisation first and giving them reasonable time to fix it before any public discussion. Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) are standard in professional engagements, legally binding the tester to confidentiality about everything discovered, including data, vulnerabilities, and client business information.

quiz.question: What is 'responsible disclosure' in the context of finding a vulnerability?
options: Immediately posting the vulnerability publicly on social media
Reporting it privately to the affected organisation and giving them time to fix it before any public discussion
Selling the vulnerability to the highest bidder
Ignoring it since it's not your problem
quiz.explanation: Responsible disclosure protects users by giving the organisation a fair chance to patch the issue before details become public, reducing the window where attackers could exploit it.

cards.title: EC-Council's Code of Ethics
cards.body: Certified Ethical Hackers agree to a formal code: keep private and confidential information gained in professional work confidential, only use techniques with proper authorisation, never engage in malicious hacking, ensure all disclosed vulnerability information is handled responsibly, and never associate with malicious hackers or engage in any activity that might damage the reputation of the profession.

cards.title: Related Certifications & Career Paths
cards.body: Beyond CEH, common industry certifications include OSCP (Offensive Security Certified Professional — hands-on, exam-based penetration testing), CompTIA Security+ (foundational, vendor-neutral entry point), and CISSP (broader security management, common for senior roles). Career paths branch into Penetration Tester/Red Team (offensive), SOC Analyst/Blue Team (defensive), and Security Consultant/Auditor (compliance-focused) — all requiring the same legal and ethical grounding covered in this unit.

quiz.question: According to the CEH Code of Ethics, what should a certified ethical hacker do with confidential information gained during professional work?
options: Publish it as a case study without permission
quiz.explanation: Maintaining strict confidentiality of all information encountered during professional engagements is a core pillar of the CEH Code of Ethics.

Reconnaissance, Scanning, Gaining Access, Maintaining Access, Covering Tracks, Reporting
Reporting, Access, Scanning, Recon, Tracks, Persistence
Access, Recon, Scanning, Report, Tracks, Persistence
quiz.explanation: The standard methodology follows: Reconnaissance → Scanning → Gaining Access → Maintaining Access → Covering Tracks → Reporting.

quiz.question: What is a 'vulnerability' in cybersecurity terms?
options: A tool used to attack a system
A weakness or flaw in a system that can be exploited
quiz.explanation: A vulnerability is a flaw or weakness — like outdated software or a weak password — that an attacker can exploit.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 17

quiz.question: Which Google Dork operator restricts search results to a specific website domain?
quiz.explanation: The 'site:' operator limits search results to a single specified domain.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 18
cards.body: This is question 18 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: What does 'Enumeration' involve in the reconnaissance/scanning process?
options: Collecting detailed information like usernames, shared folders, and software versions
quiz.explanation: Enumeration is an active info-gathering step that pulls specific, detailed data about a target system.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 19
cards.body: This is question 19 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: What is the single most important output of a professional penetration test?
options: A detailed report with findings and remediation steps
Access to the most systems possible
quiz.explanation: The report — documenting what was found and how to fix it — is the actual deliverable clients pay for, not the exploitation itself.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 20
cards.body: This is question 20 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: Which Nmap flag performs a stealthy 'half-open' SYN scan?
quiz.explanation: -sS sends a SYN packet without completing the handshake, making it faster and less likely to be logged than a full connect scan.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 21
cards.body: This is question 21 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: What does the 'Filtered' port state in Nmap output usually indicate?
options: A firewall is blocking Nmap from determining the true state
quiz.explanation: Filtered means a firewall or packet filter is interfering, preventing Nmap from confirming whether the port is open or closed.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 22
cards.body: This is question 22 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: Which Nmap flag scans all 65,535 ports on a target?
quiz.explanation: -p- is shorthand for -p 1-65535, telling Nmap to check every possible port rather than the default top 1000.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 23
cards.body: This is question 23 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the Nmap Scripting Engine (NSE)?
options: To extend Nmap with automated deeper checks like vulnerability detection
To only add color to the terminal
quiz.explanation: NSE runs Lua scripts for tasks beyond basic scanning, such as detecting known vulnerabilities or testing default credentials.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 24
cards.body: This is question 24 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: Which type of network spans an entire country or the globe?
quiz.explanation: A Wide Area Network (WAN) covers the largest geographical scale — the Internet itself is the biggest example.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 25
cards.body: This is question 25 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between a Switch and a Hub?
options: A Switch sends data only to the intended device; a Hub broadcasts to all ports
A Hub is faster than a Switch
They are exactly the same device
quiz.explanation: A Switch intelligently directs traffic only to its intended recipient, while a Hub broadcasts to every connected device.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 26
cards.body: This is question 26 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: What does DNS primarily do?
options: Translates domain names into numeric IP addresses
quiz.explanation: DNS acts as the internet's phonebook, converting human-readable names into the IP addresses computers actually use.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 27
cards.body: This is question 27 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: What is the main security benefit of using a VPN?
options: Creates an encrypted tunnel and hides your real IP address
Replaces the need for any password
quiz.explanation: A VPN encrypts traffic through a secure tunnel and masks the user's real IP, protecting data especially on untrusted networks.

options: Always use the fastest scan settings
Never test tools or attacks on networks you don't own or have written permission for
quiz.explanation: Practicing only within your own authorized lab environment is both an ethical and legal requirement.

quiz.question: In Bridged networking mode, where does a VM get its IP address from?
options: It never gets an IP address
The same DHCP server as your physical host machine
quiz.explanation: A bridged VM behaves like a separate physical device on the LAN, requesting an IP from the same DHCP server as the host.

quiz.question: Why should you never run 'apt update' on Metasploitable2?
options: It would remove the intentional vulnerabilities the machine is designed to have
It requires a different package manager
It has no internet access at all
quiz.explanation: Metasploitable2 is deliberately kept vulnerable for training — patching it would defeat its entire purpose.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 31

quiz.question: What must be running before Metasploit's database features (like db_nmap) will work?
quiz.explanation: Metasploit stores scan results and sessions in a PostgreSQL database, which must be started before use.

quiz.question: In Maltego, what is a 'Transform'?
options: A query that expands an entity to reveal new connected data
quiz.explanation: Transforms are the core mechanism in Maltego — running one pulls in new related data about an entity.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 33
cards.body: This is question 33 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: How does OpenVAS differ from Nmap?
options: Nmap discovers hosts/ports; OpenVAS checks those services against known vulnerabilities
OpenVAS only works on web applications
Nmap finds vulnerabilities; OpenVAS finds open ports
quiz.explanation: Nmap answers 'what's open?' while OpenVAS answers 'given what's open, what's actually vulnerable?'

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 34
cards.body: This is question 34 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between a Capture Filter and a Display Filter in Wireshark?
options: Capture filters decide what gets recorded; display filters narrow what's shown from already-captured data
Display filters only work on saved files
Capture filters only work on HTTP traffic
quiz.explanation: Capture filters apply before packets are saved; display filters narrow the view of already-captured data.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 35
cards.body: This is question 35 of 50 in your Final Assessment. Each question is worth 1 mark. Read carefully and select the best answer.

quiz.question: Which Burp Suite Intruder attack type tests every combination of two payload sets?
quiz.explanation: Cluster Bomb tests every combination of multiple payload sets, ideal for brute-forcing every username against every password.

quiz.question: Why does Burp Suite need its CA certificate installed in the browser's trust store?
options: To let Burp intercept and read encrypted HTTPS traffic without warnings
It's required just to open Burp
quiz.explanation: Trusting Burp's CA certificate allows it to decrypt and inspect HTTPS traffic during a proxied testing session.

quiz.question: Why are offline password attacks generally faster than online attacks?
options: They are limited only by computing power, not network speed or lockout policies
Online attacks always use stronger encryption
quiz.explanation: Offline attacks work against a captured hash file locally, unaffected by network latency or account lockout protections.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 38

quiz.question: Why is Meterpreter considered harder to detect than a traditional payload?
options: It uses a different color scheme
It runs entirely in memory rather than being written to disk
It doesn't communicate with the attacker
quiz.explanation: Running in-memory rather than writing to disk means Meterpreter leaves fewer traditional forensic traces.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 39

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of a Command & Control (C2) channel?
options: To let an attacker remotely direct a compromised system after it 'calls home'
quiz.explanation: A C2 channel is the attacker's remote control mechanism for directing compromised machines that periodically check in.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 40

quiz.question: Why is a completely empty log file often MORE suspicious to investigators than a normal one?
options: A total absence of expected entries is itself a red flag indicating deliberate tampering
Empty logs mean the system was never used
quiz.explanation: Because logs are expected to contain routine activity, a total gap stands out as unusual and prompts closer investigation.

cards.title: Final Exam — Question 41

quiz.question: What makes Spear Phishing more dangerous than generic Mass Phishing?
options: It's sent to more people at once
It's highly personalized using researched details, making it far more credible
It only targets computers, not people
quiz.explanation: Spear phishing uses researched personal details (often via OSINT) to make the message far more believable and effective.

Professional cannot run on Kali Linux

John the Ripper is always faster
quiz.explanation: Hydra performs online brute-forcing over the network, while offline tools crack an already-captured hash file.

options: How aggressive/potentially destructive the tested payloads are
quiz.explanation: Higher risk levels include payloads more likely to alter data, requiring greater caution and authorization.

options: It's too slow for modern devices
It has fundamental cryptographic weaknesses crackable in minutes regardless of password strength
quiz.explanation: WEP's encryption design is fundamentally broken and can be cracked quickly using well-known techniques.

quiz.question: Within how many hours must a data breach be reported under GDPR?

quiz.question: What is 'responsible disclosure' when a vulnerability is discovered?
options: Immediately posting it publicly on social media
Reporting it privately to the affected organization and giving them time to fix it first
Selling it to the highest bidder
quiz.explanation: Responsible disclosure protects users by giving the organization a fair chance to patch the issue before public details could be exploited.
